In its FY2024 10-K, Boeing reported that financing cash flows of $25.2 billion in 2024 were primarily driven by the issuance of common stock and Mandatory convertible preferred stock in the fourth quarter of 2024, which resulted in cash proceeds of $18.2 billion and $5.7 billion, net of issuance costs [1]. Boeing also issued $10.0 billion of fixed-rate senior notes in the second quarter of 2024, with net borrowings of $1.5 billion for the full year [1].

In the second quarter of 2024, Boeing entered into a $4.0 billion five-year revolving credit agreement expiring in May 2029 [2]. Also in the second quarter of 2024, Boeing terminated the $0.8 billion 364-day revolving credit agreement scheduled to expire in August 2024, and the $3.2 billion five-year revolving credit agreement, as amended, scheduled to expire in October 2024 [2][3]. At December 31, 2024, Boeing had $10.0 billion available under credit line agreements and remained in full compliance with all debt covenants, though Moody's had downgraded its short-term and long-term credit ratings to Baa3/P-3 in April 2024 [2][3].

In its FY2025 10-K, Boeing disclosed that in August 2025 it entered into a $3.0 billion, 364-day revolving credit agreement expiring in August 2026, replacing the $3.0 billion three-year revolving credit agreement which was scheduled to terminate in August 2025, with a one-year term out option allowing extension of any borrowings until August 2027 [4]. The legacy $3.0 billion five-year revolving credit agreement expiring in August 2028 and $4.0 billion five-year revolving credit agreement expiring in May 2029 each remained in effect, leaving $10.0 billion of unused borrowing capacity at December 31, 2025 [4]. In connection with the Spirit Acquisition completed in December 2025, Boeing assumed Spirit's remaining debt, including $300 of 3.850% Senior Notes due 2026, $700 of 4.600% Senior Notes due 2028, and $230 of 3.250% Exchangeable Notes due 2028 [5].

Net cash used by financing activities in 2025 was $3.8 billion, primarily driven by net repayments of $3.5 billion, with total debt balances at December 31, 2025 and 2024 totaling $54.1 billion and $53.9 billion, of which $8.5 billion and $1.3 billion were classified as short-term [6]. By the end of 2025, all three major rating agencies had revised Boeing's outlooks to stable from negative: Fitch affirmed the BBB- credit rating in June 2025, S&P affirmed the BBB- credit rating in October 2025, and Moody's affirmed the Baa3 credit rating in December 2025 [4].
